liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Jerry's vocal attempt in the Dew falls short for this reviewer; Reviewer, after years of searching late-80s Dews, rates this the best Morning Dew they have heard [10][15]
- **Big Boss Man** (1 review): Opening version is described as loose and sloppy, with Jerry sounding sluggish [9]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Reviewer thought the band might fumble the ending of Stranger, but they pulled it off [13]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer calls it decent but cautions about Bobby's slide playing; also notes a nod to Oakland [9]
- **All Along The Watchtower (Tape Paused Till Encore)** (1 review): Reviewer finds Watchtower a weak way to end the show [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Push Comes To Shove**: cut on the recording [18]
- **Thank You,Goodnight!**: rare: 5 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-11-06.AudUnk.White.Keo.116460.Flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 147 min [1]. Said about its sound: Audience source captures lots of audience participation [1]
- **gd1987-11-06.AudUnk.White.Keo.116459.Flac2496**: source not stated; 19 songs; 147 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the files on the audience recording don't seem to match the actual setlist order [12]
- **gd87-11-06.sbd.miller.11656.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 145 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Audio during the first set's Uncle and Cumberland is reported as coming from only one ear/channel [9]
- **gd1987-11-06.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83941.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 146 min [5]
- **gd1987-11-06.166967.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 150 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the band had just returned from a month off, with bad transitions, missed notes and an odd setlist [10]
- Rex Benefit show; fans chanted for Phil, and the lights came on but the crowd stayed [1]
- The band returned for an encore after the crowd refused to leave [1]
- Reviewer considers the show fairly ordinary compared with typical 1987 performances [8]
- Reviewer saw Jerry decline from 1984 to 1986 and welcomed his better state in 1987 shows [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-11-06.AudUnk.White.Keo.116460.Flac1644**: taped by Mr. White; transferred by Keo; source: First Generation Cassettes From Unknown Mics/Deck>Unknown Original Copy Decks/Info; Tapes From White,Transfer By Keo; Tapes Maxell XLII Gold 90's; Transfer… [1]
- **gd1987-11-06.AudUnk.White.Keo.116459.Flac2496**: taped by Mr. White; transferred by Keo; source: First Generation Cassettes From Unknown Mics/Deck>Unknown Original Copy Decks/Info; Tapes From White,Transfer By Keo; Tapes Maxell XLII Gold 90's; Transfer… [2]
- **gd87-11-06.sbd.miller.11656.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>Cm>Dat>Samplitude>Cool Edit Pro>CD [3]
- **gd1987-11-06.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83941.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [5]. Also: Complete show made from two soundboard cassette masters, from tapes by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [5]
- **gd1987-11-06.166967.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S90) [6]. Also: A White and Keo audience source supplies a 1:08 patch in Space; Wheel space is included in The Wheel [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-11-08 Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-11-08-henry-j-kaiser-convention-center-oakland-ca-usa/) [19]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center - November 7, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/november-7-1987) [20]
